statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. The Nasdaq-100 venue is inside the CME weekend halt and Tail remains well below the block threshold.
recommendation: The mapped policy state stays EA_ON across all 24 hours because every slot falls inside the weekend closure and no price path can form. No danger window is defined. The next evidence checkpoint is the Globex reopen on Sunday 30 August at 22:00 UTC, which lies beyond this window; opening structure would be assessed on observed evidence in a later run.
headline: Weekend CME halt holds after a hawkish Jackson Hole Friday: NQ settled 29,509.50, cash NDX -0.70%, VIX 14.43
body: CME Globex has been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and does not reopen until Sunday 30 August at 22:00 UTC, so every hour of this forecast window is a closed market with no Nasdaq-100 price discovery. Verified pre-halt evidence: NQ futures settled 29,509.50 (-0.63%) inside a 29,436.75-29,811.50 range, cash NDX closed 29,433.43 (-0.70%) in a 29,383.92-29,752.78 range, and VIX finished at 14.43 within a 14.13-14.84 range. Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote was read as hawkish on inflation and moved September rate-hike odds from roughly 35% to about 60%, with the 2-year yield reported up about 11 basis points to 4.34% and the 10-year up about 5 basis points to 4.72%, against official H.15 readings for 27 August of 2Y 4.20% and 10Y 4.67%. Friday's internals were dispersed rather than aligned: delayed latest-session context shows five of eight megacaps higher, with Amazon near +4.0% and Microsoft, Alphabet and Apple each up more than 1.5%, set against a semiconductor de-rating in which all seven tracked names fell, led by Arm near -6.3% and Nvidia near -4.6%. Sector context is a rotation, with Technology near -1.4% against Communication Services and Consumer Cyclical each near +1.4%. Energy is easing rather than escalating: WTI settled near $83.44 and Brent near $88.29, extending a weekly decline of roughly 4%, with Persian Gulf exports reported recovering toward 15-16 million barrels per day. One new weekend headline, an announced US-Venezuela oil arrangement published after the halt began, reached no tradeable venue and is carried as gap exposure rather than as current structure. Because Tail measures a persistent no-retracement price path and no venue exists in which such a path could form, Tail is held at 5 for every hour of the window. Stress runs 22 to 27, crossing into the moderate band around Saturday midday, to carry the unresolved September policy question and the 1-4 September catalyst stack of ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS, ADP, jobless claims and trade balance, ISM Services and August payrolls. Confidence eases from 82 to 76 purely as the verified Friday prints age.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours cover Friday's full session and the first hours of the weekend halt. Tail ran 11-13 with Stress in the high 40s to mid 50s through the Asian and European hours as positioning built ahead of the Jackson Hole keynote. Tail peaked at 22 and Stress at 64 in the 16:00-19:00 UTC block, when the hawkish keynote drove event-driven two-way trade and the mode was scored event/whipsaw; the mapped policy state never exceeded WATCH because retracements kept occurring. After the 20:00 UTC cash close the readings decayed quickly, Tail from 12 to 5 and Stress from 52 to 23, as the venue entered the weekend closure and the mode reverted to normal. One hour, 10:00 UTC on 28 August, has no published assessment and is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: Every hour of the forecast window falls inside the CME weekend halt, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form and Tail is held at 5 in all 24 slots, keeping the mapped policy state at EA_ON throughout with no danger window. Stress runs 22 to 27, crossing from the low into the moderate band around Saturday midday to carry the unresolved September policy repricing and the 1-4 September catalyst stack of ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS, ADP, jobless claims and trade balance, ISM Services and August payrolls. Confidence eases from 82 to 76 purely as Friday's verified prints age; the shared cross-asset context is fresh and confirms dispersed rather than aligned internals, which keeps the exposure in Stress rather than Tail. The dominant mode is normal in every slot because a closed market has no structure to classify. Weekend headline and gap exposure accumulates, including the announced US-Venezuela oil arrangement, but it can only be priced at the Sunday 22:00 UTC reopen, which lies beyond this window.

A closed venue offers no structure for mean reversion to fail against.

news.title: Stock market today: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq moderate as markets digest Warsh's Jackson Hole speech

forecast.analysis: The unresolved input carried into this hour is Friday's rate repricing, not a price path. Reuters reported September hike odds moving from about 35% to roughly 60% after the Jackson Hole keynote, with the 2-year yield up about 11bp to 4.34% and the 10-year up about 5bp to 4.72%. That is a Stress and Confidence input while the venue stays shut.

2Y yield +11bp to ~4.34%, its highest in a month; 10Y +5bp to ~4.72%
Rate repricing without a tradeable venue informs Stress, not Tail

forecast.analysis: Official benchmarks lag the market print: H.15 shows 2Y 4.20% and 10Y 4.67% as of 27 August, against Friday's reported 4.34% and 4.72%. The gap is a known measurement lag rather than a discrepancy. No hourly reassessment of the curve is possible before the official series updates next week.

Friday market prints ran above the official series; lag is expected

forecast.analysis: Asian hours on a Saturday carry no Nasdaq-100 cash or futures venue, so any directional read this hour would rest on unobserved structure. Tail stays at 5 because a closed market cannot produce shallow pullbacks, failed retracements or repeated extension. Cross-asset context remains the delayed latest-session snapshot.

Tail held at 5: no venue in which mean reversion could fail
Cross-asset context is delayed latest-session, not a live price path

forecast.analysis: Friday's internals were dispersed rather than aligned, which conditions how a later reopen would be scored. Delayed latest-session context shows five of eight megacaps higher, Amazon near +4.0% with Microsoft +1.7%, Alphabet +1.7% and Apple +1.6%, against Nvidia near -4.6%. Dispersion of that kind argues against a one-way tape.

Nvidia ~-4.6% and Tesla ~-1.7% offset the hyperscaler bid

news.title: Stock market today: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq moderate as markets digest Warsh's Jackson Hole speech

forecast.analysis: The semiconductor leg is the clearest single-sector move in the pre-halt session: all seven tracked names lower, Arm near -6.3%, Nvidia near -4.6%, Intel near -2.9% and AMD near -2.3%, with Semiconductor Equipment & Materials near -4.0%. That is a sector de-rating inside a rotation, and it would only matter for Tail if the index itself later trended one-way.
drivers: All seven tracked semis lower; ARM ~-6.3%, NVDA ~-4.6%, INTC ~-2.9%
Semiconductor Equipment & Materials industry group ~-4.0%
Sector de-rating alone is not index-level one-way structure

forecast.analysis: Breadth context describes rotation rather than a broad risk-off impulse: Technology near -1.4% against Communication Services near +1.4% and Consumer Cyclical near +1.4%, with application and infrastructure software both slightly positive. Conflicting breadth lowers directional conviction, so it informs Stress rather than raising Tail.
drivers: Technology ~-1.4% vs Communication Services ~+1.4%, Consumer Cyclical ~+1.4%
Software - Application ~+0.4% and Software - Infrastructure ~+0.2% held up
Conflicting breadth reduces conviction; it does not mechanically raise Tail

forecast.analysis: Volatility pricing entered the halt contained. VIX settled 14.43 within a 14.13-14.84 range, and the delayed VIX futures context shows only a modest session gain of about 1.6%. A low volatility base means any weekend repricing would start from a compressed level, which is a Stress consideration for the reopen rather than a current-hour condition.
drivers: VIX settled 14.43 in a 14.13-14.84 range; implied volatility compressed
Delayed VX futures context ~+1.6% on the session, a modest bid
A compressed base is a reopen consideration, not a current-hour signal

forecast.analysis: Energy is a stabilising rather than escalating input this hour. WTI settled near $83.44 (-0.11%) and Brent near $88.29 (-0.26%), extending a weekly decline of roughly 4%, with Persian Gulf exports reported recovering toward 15-16 million barrels per day. Absent an energy shock, the geopolitical channel into Nasdaq-100 Tail stays weak.
drivers: Persian Gulf exports reported recovering to ~15-16 mb/d
No live energy discontinuity to transmit into index Tail

forecast.analysis: The one genuinely new weekend headline is an announced US-Venezuela oil arrangement covering a large reserve share, published after the halt began. It reached no tradeable venue and its market transmission is an energy-supply story rather than a Nasdaq-100 mechanism, so it is logged as gap exposure to reassess when Globex reopens.

Headline hit no tradeable venue; transmission is via energy supply

It is a scheduled item only; no outcome is known or assumed. Stress holds at 26 to carry the labour-week exposure while Tail stays anchored at 5 through the closure.

On the calibration used here a payrolls surprise primarily raises Stress and Confidence dispersion rather than Tail, and Tail would only move on an observed no-retracement path after the release, far beyond this window.
